title: Why Afterimages Appear After Bright Lights: It's Not What You Think
hook: Your eyes get tired, just like your muscles.

narration.text: Your eyes get tired, just like your muscles.
When you stare at a bright light, the photoreceptors in your retina work hard.
These cells become overstimulated, especially the ones detecting that specific colour.
This overstimulation leads to something called retinal fatigue.
When you look away, those fatigued cells respond less to new light.
Other, rested cells take over, creating an inverted, phantom afterimage.
This is why a bright red light leaves a green afterimage, for instance.
It is your brain trying to balance out the visual input.
Have you ever noticed strong afterimages after looking at a screen?

description: Ever wondered why you see strange colours after looking at a bright light? It's all about how your eyes' photoreceptors get tired. Learn about retinal fatigue and the fascinating way your brain balances visual information.
topic: Why you sometimes see an afterimage when you look away from a bright light, explaining retinal fatigue.
